title: Graves' Hyperthyroidism — Young Female with Anxiety, Palpitations, Tremor
patient: Young female, anxiety, palpitations, tremor, sweating, exophthalmos, pretibial myxedema, large thyroid on exam
hpi: Young woman presents with anxiety, palpitations, tremor, sweating. Physical exam reveals large thyroid, mild exophthalmos, pretibial myxedema, fine tremor.

exam.relevant: Large thyroid, mild exophthalmos, tremor, pretibial myxedema

missed.why: Any woman of childbearing age needs pregnancy status before anti-thyroid meds. Methimazole is teratogenic in first trimester (aplasia cutis, choanal atresia, esophageal atresia). PTU is preferred in first trimester. This is the single most critical miss.

Thyroid hormone directly increases sinoatrial node firing rate, shortens atrial refractory period, and increases sympathetic sensitivity. Result: sinus tachycardia and atrial fibrillation risk. ECG screens for rate, rhythm, and any ischemic changes from demand ischemia.
Anxiety, palpitations, tremor = classic stimulant toxidrome (cocaine, methamphetamine). Must rule out before committing to endocrine diagnosis.
Graves' is autoimmune. Methimazole and PTU both carry risk of agranulocytosis — need baseline WBC before starting. Also screen for anemia of chronic disease.
PTU carries black box warning for fulminant hepatic necrosis. Baseline LFTs mandatory. CMP for renal function (drug clearance) and electrolytes.

Beta-blocker treats symptoms only. Definitive treatment requires blocking new thyroid hormone synthesis. Methimazole inhibits thyroid peroxidase (TPO), preventing iodination of thyroglobulin. PTU does the same PLUS blocks peripheral T4→T3 conversion (5'-deiodinase).
Graves' management is nuanced: titration vs block-and-replace, monitoring for agranulocytosis, timing of definitive therapy (RAI vs surgery). Endocrine should be involved from day 1.

mechanism.graves: Autoantibodies (TSI — thyroid-stimulating immunoglobulins) bind TSH receptor on thyroid follicular cells → constitutive activation → uncontrolled T4/T3 production → negative feedback suppresses pituitary TSH → TSH is low/near-zero, free T4/T3 are elevated
mechanism.heart: T3 directly enters cardiomyocytes via MCT8 transporter → binds nuclear thyroid hormone receptor → upregulates: beta-1 adrenergic receptors (increased catecholamine sensitivity), sarcoplasmic reticulum Ca2+-ATPase (faster relaxation, shorter diastolic filling), myosin heavy chain alpha isoform (faster contraction velocity). Net effect: increased heart rate, increased contractility, shortened atrial refractory period → atrial fibrillation risk.
mechanism.eye: TSI cross-reacts with orbital fibroblasts → fibroblast activation → glycosaminoglycan deposition → retro-orbital tissue expansion → proptosis/exophthalmos. Same mechanism in pretibial area → pretibial myxedema.
mechanism.beta_blocker: Propranolol is non-selective beta-1 + beta-2 blockade. At high doses also blocks 5'-monodeiodinase (T4→T3 conversion) — minimal clinical effect, takes ~10 days. Real benefit: slows HR, reduces tremor, decreases anxiety. Atenolol/metoprolol (beta-1 selective) equally effective, better tolerated.
mechanism.methimazole_vs_ptu: Methimazole: once-daily dosing, faster euthyroid state, less hepatotoxicity. Contraindicated in first trimester (teratogenic). PTU: three-times-daily dosing, blocks peripheral T4→T3 conversion (bonus), black box for hepatic necrosis. Preferred in first trimester ONLY. Both carry agranulocytosis risk (~0.3%).

timing.note: Case timed out before correct diagnosis and treatment
